one.question: Can the same action have different intentions? Give one everyday example.
one.answer: Yes. Two people can help with housework: one may want to support their family, while another may want praise. The action is similar, but the intention is different.

two.question: Describe one helpful action you could do today. What is your intention?
two.answer: I can help a classmate understand a task. My intention is to be useful and kind, not to receive attention.

overview.title: What this lesson will help you do
overview.purpose: Connect an action with the reason behind it, understand the Hadith's main message, and explain a personal purpose in clear English.
overview.goal: Explain an action and its intention

message.title: Understand
message.description: Identify the main message without making detailed religious rulings.

words.title: Build vocabulary
words.description: Learn action, intention, motive, migrate, worldly gain, and connected expressions.

language.title: Express purpose
language.description: Use to, in order to, and because accurately.

transfer.title: Use it
transfer.description: Give a short, clear example from everyday life.

warmup.title: One action, different reasons
warmup.description: Start with a familiar situation. There is no score here—the goal is to notice the difference between an action and its intention.
warmup.scenario: Two people help clean the same room.
warmup.prompt: One wants to support the family. The other wants a reward. Their action looks the same, but their reasons are different.
warmup.question: What changes between the two people?
warmup.feedback: The action can look identical while the intention changes. Keep that contrast in mind as you read and listen.

intend.meaning: plan to carry out an action

motive.meaning: the internal reason behind an action

speak.title: Explain an action and its intention
speak.description: Choose a helpful or neutral everyday action. Speak for two or three sentences; your response is private and is not stored.
speak.frame: I [action]. I did it because [reason]. My intention was to [purpose].
speak.model: I helped my sibling with their studies. I did it because the homework was difficult. My intention was to help them understand.

checks.language: I used to, because, intention, or motive.
checks.clarity: My pronunciation was easy to understand.

review.title: Retrieve, check, and plan your review
review.description: Answer from memory before opening each model answer. This strengthens recall more than rereading.

message.question: What is the main message of the Hadith?
message.answer: An action is connected to the intention or motive behind it.

words.question: Can you explain the five core expressions?
words.answer: Action is a deed; intention is a plan or purpose; motive is the internal reason; migrate means move to another place; worldly gain is a material benefit.

connectors.question: How do to, in order to, and because express purpose or reason?
connectors.answer: Use to or in order to before a verb: I study to learn. Use because before a clause: I study because I want to learn.

transfer.question: Give a two-sentence everyday example.
transfer.answer: I called my friend because they felt worried. My intention was to support them.
